I’ve worked in the Health Insurance industry for 30+ years.  I now volunteer in helping senior select the best plan for their specific situation.  I’m surprised how complicated Medicare and Medicare supplement/Medicare Advantage  products are. You have to review your plan every year.  Plans go out of business in the middle of a calendar year, drugs may no longer be covered or prior authorization may suddenly be required.  When they do go out of business, you may get just an email which can be easily be overlooked.  

One thing I don’t think people understand is the millions of dollar doctors and hospitals write off each year.  Insurance companies will continue to deny claims until the timely filing deadline has passed.  If a provider fails to get the prior authorization, the provider has to write the charges off.
